papers.title: Coefficient choice in Galois-ring lifts of APN permutations: sharp unit-direction spectra and one-term optimal lifts
papers.abstract: Permutation polynomials over the Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ are nonlinear components for symmetric primitives that add keys in the ring, as in secure computation modulo $2^k$. R{\o}njom and Sandrib showed that their differential uniformity is at least $2q^{k-1}$, where $q=2^m$. For the class studied here it is attained on top-layer differences, while almost all differences are units. We ask how small the difference table can be on unit differences when the residue permutation is fixed and only higher coefficient digits of its lift are chosen. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, $k\ge3$, and let $p$ be a reduced quadratic almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ whose derivative is nowhere zero and two-to-one. Over all lifts of $p$, the least possible maximum on unit differences is $q$ or $2q$, decided by two invariants of $p$ and the level $k$. We describe every lift attaining it and show that the coefficients modulo $8$ decide optimality at every level. For every odd $m\ge5$, residue permutations with at most $16$ monomials attain $q$ after one $2$-adic digit of one coefficient of the natural lift is changed. For an explicit infinite family, one added monomial lowers the maximum on unit differences from $4q$, or from at least $q^2$, to $2q$ at every level without raising the degree. Under a uniform starting state and independent uniform round keys, valuation preservation yields layerwise bounds for characteristics and two-round differentials that distinguish lifts with the same global uniformity. Core results are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Re-Ordering the Generalized Hofstadter Functions G, H, and Beyond
papers.abstract: Hofstadter's G function is recursively defined via G(0) = 0 and then G(n) = n-G(G(n -1)). Following Hofstadter, we vary the number k of nested recursive calls in this equation and obtain a family of functions (F\_k). In a previous article, we proved that this family is ordered pointwise: for all k and n, we have $F_k(n) $le$ F_{k+1}(n)$. Here we propose a much shorter proof of this theorem, without infinite morphic words. The key ingredient for this direct proof is a new formula expressing iterates of the preimages of $F_k$ . Thanks to this formula, we also prove several conjectures mentioned in our previous article. In particular we obtain that $F_k(n) < F_{k+1}(n)$ when n > (k + 1)(k + 6)/2. We provide a certified formalization of all these results in the Rocq proof assistant.

papers.title: Resolvent Components of Completely Normal Elements and the Morgan-Mullen Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study completely normal elements of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, that is, elements that are normal over every intermediate field, through partial Lagrange resolvents. In these coordinates, complete normality splits into independent components, in a way closely related to Hachenberger's decomposition theory. Our main tool is a structure theorem for the components; together with a finite computation, it shows that every component has weight (the sum of the probabilities that its conditions fail) at most $3/4$, uniformly in $n$. Combined with the classical character-sum method, this gives an explicit sufficient criterion for the existence of a primitive completely normal element. We verify the criterion for all $n>q$ except $70$ pairs $(q,n)$, which we settle with explicit elements found by computer. Since the case $n\le q$ is due to Garefalakis and Kapetanakis, this confirms the conjecture of Morgan and Mullen (1996) that every $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ contains a primitive element that is completely normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$. The same estimates give two further results. First, Hachenberger's conjectured lower bound $(q-1)^{n'}q^{(p^a-1)n'}$ for the number of completely normal elements, where $p$ is the characteristic and $n=p^an'$ with $p\nmid n'$, holds for all pairs $(q,n)$; it was known for regular pairs. Second, primitivity and complete normality are asymptotically independent: as $q^n\to\infty$, the number of primitive completely normal elements is $(1+o(1))\,\varphi(q^n-1)/(q^n-1)$ times the number of completely normal elements (for fixed $n$ this was known). Our arguments for $n>q$ and for both further results, including every computer-assisted step, are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the formalisation takes the case $n\le q$ and an explicit bound of Rosser and Schoenfeld as axioms and relies on Lean's compiler and interpreter for the large computations.

papers.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
papers.abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

papers.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
papers.abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

papers.title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
papers.abstract: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$. Both bounds are independent of the coefficient field, and these analytic models require no coefficient extension. A prescribed absolute Frobenius structure extends to such a bounded model with the same radius and connection bound. After a finite coefficient extension, we also realize quasi-constant modules, which carry the finite local monodromy, as differential direct summands of sums of pushforwards of rank-one modules, with uniformly bounded cover degrees and highest breaks of the inducing modules.

papers.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
papers.abstract: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.

papers.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
papers.abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

papers.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
papers.abstract: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.

papers.title: Automorphic functions for nilpotent extensions of curves over finite fields
papers.abstract: We define and study the subspace of cuspidal functions for $G$-bundles (and its ramified analogs) on a class of nilpotent extensions of curves over a finite field. In the case of length $2$ extensions and of $G=\mathrm{GL}_2$, we prove that the space of cuspidal functions (for bundles with a fixed determinant) is finite-dimensional and provide bounds on its dimension. In this case we also relate cuspidality to Hecke finiteness, defined in terms of the action of some natural Hecke operators. Finally, we construct some Hecke eigenfunctions using the relation to Higgs bundles over the corresponding reduced curve.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Motives from Toric Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two compactifications of general hypersurfaces defined by the vanishing of linear combinations of $d+2$ monomials in $d$-dimensional algebraic tori. We prove that the number of their $\mathbb{F}_q$-points is given by finite hypergeometric sums under certain general conditions. In the process, we introduce the notion of a gamma triple, which allows us to extend the classical definition of finite hypergeometric sums to prime powers corresponding to the cyclotomic field of definition of the associated monodromy representation. As a special case of our main results, we study the Dwork family and obtain a formula for the number of its $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. Our results generalise the work of Beukers, Cohen, and Mellit for finite hypergeometric sums defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Jack multiple zeta function
papers.abstract: For conjugate shapes $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_\lambda(x;\alpha)$ and $J_{\lambda'}(x;1/\alpha)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by step along chains of partitions. Since the duality is an identity among formal symbols, the same duality holds when the multiple zeta functions are replaced by other functions, and replacing them with the monomial quasi-symmetric functions recovers Stanley's duality. Hence our duality is a refinement of Stanley's duality which contains it as a special case. In particular, we obtain a duality for the Schur multiple zeta functions and the classical relation between the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions. We next show that any expansion of a Jack symmetric function in terms of Schur functions can be lifted to Jack multiple zeta functions, yielding an analog of a formula conjectured by Stanley and proved by Koike. We also show that the Jack multiple zeta functions of one-row shape give a one-parameter family interpolating the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions, and we discuss their values at $\{2\}^r$ and at $\{2\}^a,3,\{2\}^b$.

papers.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
papers.abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

papers.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.

papers.title: Hankel determinants for the $(n+2)$-shifted $q$-metallic numbers
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $q$-deformation (in the sense of Morier-Genoud & Ovsienko) of the metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$. This is a power series with integer coefficients. We prove that the Hankel continued fraction of the $(n+2)$-shifted series $\Phi_n^{(n+2)}$ is eventually periodic, and that the corresponding Hankel determinant sequence $\Delta^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic if $n$ is even, $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic if $n$ is odd, and that it takes only the values $-2,-1,0,1,2$. This confirms part of a former conjecture of ours and complements similar results we obtained for all $\ell$-shifts of $\Phi_n$ with $0\le\ell\le n+1$. In addition, we formulate a new conjecture of quasi-polynomiality for higher shifts $\ell\ge n+3$. The determinant values arise as telescoping products of the partial numerators of the Hankel continued fraction. Most of the technically involved and lengthy verifications are carried out by a symbolic computation program, whose code is publicly available on GitHub for independent verification.

papers.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
papers.abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the H\"older Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each H\"older semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the H\"older Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the H\"older semicomplexes that can be realized as a H\"older Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.

papers.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
papers.abstract: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ \tau_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation. The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; \tau_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.

papers.title: Arithmetic Poisson summation formulas
papers.abstract: We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $\zeta(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $\zeta$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.

papers.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
papers.abstract:
For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=	au(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $
u_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p
mid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. We call $n$ \emph{matchable} if $D(n)$ admits a coprime matching with the primitive arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. The general criterion implies that $n$ is matchable if and only if $\lfloor N/pfloor\le N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We explicitly classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. A Vandermonde determinant gives the required matchings under bounds on the prime exponents, while a partition into shorter progressions handles the remaining cases.

papers.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

papers.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
papers.abstract: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

papers.title: Infinite families and sporadic solutions of the equation $\varphi(n)=c+\alpha\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$
papers.abstract: Ranjan and Singh proved that for every composite $n$ which is not twice an odd prime, $\varphi(n)$ is at least one plus the sum of $\varphi$ over the prime divisors of $n$, with equality exactly for $n=4,12,30$. \new{We study the weighted equation $\varphi(n)=c+\alpha\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$. We determine the parameters $(c,\alpha)$ admitting infinite families of solutions, prove that all remaining solutions are finite in number and arise from an explicit linear mechanism, and compute them exactly in a range of parameters; the finiteness of $\{4,12,30\}$ becomes a special case. We also settle the analogous equations for the divisor functions $\tau$ and $\sigma$ and for the Jordan totients, and, from known results on the sum of the prime divisors, derive the full asymptotic expansion of the average deficiency.} \K{In the range $|c|\le10$, $1\le\alpha\le6$ the composite solution set is determined completely\V{, and the number and the size of the sporadic solutions are shown to be bounded by polynomials in $|c|+\alpha$}.} \B{Finally, replacing the prime values $\varphi(p)$ by their iterates $\varphi^{(k)}(p)$, we determine all solutions of $\varphi(n)=1+\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi^{(k)}(p)$: the solution sets are $\{1,4,12,30\}$, $\{1,3,4,10\}$ and, for every $k\ge3$, $\{1,3,4\}$; for the weighted iterated equation we exhibit an infinite family governed by the safe primes.

papers.title: Retriangular numbers and affine maps between polygonal numbers
papers.abstract: A positive integer $a$ is called \emph{retriangular} if there is a positive integer $b$ such that $aT+b$ is a triangular number whenever $T$ is. We show that the retriangular numbers are exactly the odd squares greater than $1$, and that for each of them $b$ is unique. The proof rests on a rigidity principle: a non-constant affine map carrying the values of one quadratic sequence into the values of another is induced by an affine map of the plane sending the vertex of one parabola to the vertex of the other. We use it to classify all affine maps between sets of polygonal numbers; the $s$-gonal numbers map affinely into the $t$-gonal numbers if and only if $M_t\mid M_s$, where $M_s=2(s-2)/\gcd(s,4)$ defines a bijection from $\{3,4,5,\dots\}$ onto the positive integers. We also treat sparse data, polynomial maps, figurate numbers of higher degree and sums of two triangular numbers, and we study the monoid of affine self-maps of an arbitrary set of integers. For the $s$-gonal numbers this monoid is an arithmetical congruence monoid, and the factorization of self-maps into irreducible ones is unique only for triangular and square numbers.

papers.title: Metric Diophantine approximation with primes on irrational lines
papers.abstract: Let $c>1$ be irrational. We prove that, for almost every $x>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many triples $(p,r,s)$, with $p$ and $r$ prime and $s$ an integer, for which \[ 0<px-r<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon},\qquad 0<pcx-s<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon}. \] This improves the exponent $1/5$ in the homogeneous-line case of a theorem of Baier and Ghosh. The arithmetic input is the quantitative prime-counting lower bound in Matom\"aki's proof concerning primes in shrinking neighborhoods of an irrational rotation. We obtain a local first-moment lower bound by fixing the prime numerator and applying the prime number theorem to the admissible prime denominators. Two Selberg sieve squares, together with explicit trigonometric interval approximations, give a pointwise upper bound whose error tends to zero in $L^1$ after normalization. A truncation and density-point argument then yields the almost-everywhere conclusion.

papers.title: Moment representations for generalized Lehmer polynomials
papers.abstract: We represent normalized generalized Lehmer polynomials as moments of a random variable constructed from two independent negative binomial variables and an independent uniform variable. An integral form of their known exponential generating function yields mixtures of uniform distributions and convergent double series. We recover Eulerian polynomial identities and give a probabilistic interpretation of anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. We also prove moment determinacy, characterize the Stieltjes parameter range, derive Hankel total non-negativity and log-convexity, and identify the boundary distributions.

papers.title: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
papers.abstract: We establish a uniform effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimate for abelian varieties, conditional on the Mumford-Tate conjecture and the standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the irreducible representations of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate group. The proof uses spectral majorants and minorants of indicator functions. For regions whose boundaries have finite upper (d-1)-dimensional Minkowski content, the resulting exponent improves that in Bucur et al. (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We establish uniform estimates for regions and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter, and for prime-dependent regions satisfying an explicit variation condition. As an application, we obtain a conditional upper bound for the number of primes at which a weight-two newform with a quadratic coefficient field has a rational Fourier coefficient. We also formulate a discrepancy conjecture, motivated by a probabilistic model, that implies the asymptotic predicted by Murty (Conjecture 3.4, 1999).

papers.title: Archimedean zeta integrals on $ {\rm SO}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n$ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n $
papers.abstract: We evaluate the archimedean Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals associated with spherical principal series representations of ${\rm SO}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $, where $ {\rm SO}_{2n} $ is split and $n\ge2$. We obtain explicit formulas expressing these integrals as quotients of products of gamma functions. Our approach uses Mellin-Barnes representations of spherical Whittaker functions, together with new integral identities for their Mellin transforms and transformations of Barnes integrals. In the even orthogonal case, we establish a recurrence in the rank and evaluate the integral by induction. The symplectic case then follows from an explicit identity relating the two families of zeta integrals.

papers.title: Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups
papers.abstract: Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $\Gamma_2$ we construct an explicit representation $\rho:\Gamma_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $\Gamma_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $\Gamma_g$ with $g\ge2$.

papers.title: Square-root logarithmic bounds for the arithmetic complexity of factorial multiples
papers.abstract: Assume that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in $\Re(s)>1-\delta$, $s\neq1$, for some fixed $0<\delta\leq1/2$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, a positive multiple $m_k k!$ has arithmetic complexity $\tau(m_k k!)\leq\exp(C\sqrt{\log k\log\log k})$, where $C$ depends only on $\delta$. We first establish a smooth-number asymptotic at every sufficiently large center $x$ in intervals of length at least $x^{3/4}$. Combining this estimate with an established genus-two construction yields the arithmetic bound without Cheng's conjecture on smooth numbers in elliptic Hasse intervals. The bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
